1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the user solely from the server-side session via authenticated(req), and the JSON body parser explicitly rejects any request containing userId/accountId, so settings are always scoped to the signed-in account.

2.why: The identity verification code is an HMAC bound to the specific session id (identityCode(sessionId)) and its hash is stored on that session only, so a code cannot work for any other user or session.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets mfaEnabled and rotates nothing; no other sessions for that user are deleted, so previously issued sessions remain valid until idle/absolute timeout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encryptedTotp) and backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in backupHashes, never plaintext.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, TOTP seeds, backup codes, encryption key and pepper are all generated with crypto.getRandomValues (CSPRNG).

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; only the CSRF token and displayed codes live transiently in JS memory.

7.why: Dedicated server-side validators (email, phone, password, otp, backup) with strict regexes and normalisation gate all input, and no SQL/dynamic query construction exists (in-memory Maps).

8.why: All dynamic values (setup key, backup codes, error messages, log lines) are inserted with textContent, while innerHTML is used only with static literal markup.

9.why: The only client-supplied 'destination' is accepted solely when equal to "/" (rejected otherwise) and the HTTP→HTTPS redirect uses a hard-coded internal host, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: hdr() sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() and clearCookie() both emit Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Max-Age.

12.why: Server errors are generic and no server-side secret logging occurs, but the API returns testCode, manualSecret, testCounter and backup codes in responses which the client writes into console.log and a visible on-page 'Logs' panel.

13.why: Identity codes have identityUsed plus a 5-minute identityExpires, pending TOTP has pendingTotpUsed/pendingTotpExpires and an 'accepted' counter set, and backup codes are deleted from the set on successful use.

14.why: Identity, TOTP and backup verification each increment failure counters and set a 10-minute lockout after MAX=5 failures, checked via available().

15.why: rotate() issues a new session id (and CSRF token) at sign-in and again on successful identity verification, active() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
